output.headline: TPG pays upper-quartile multiples and has 8 adjacent provider deals, but this is a low-conviction call: its median deal is under half the target's size.
output.differentiator: Pays above the comparable 75th percentile (median paid 15.7x against 15.3x) with $303.0 billion in assets under management behind it. Peer lines were not available for comparison.
output.why_them: Large sponsor paying upper-quartile multiples; adjacent provider record

acquirer_overview.title: Large sponsor with an 18-deal record, mostly outside the target's sub-sector
points: Financial sponsor with $303.0 billion in assets under management as of December 31, 2025 (TPG Inc.); its home sub-sector is Health Insurance. [P:1, B:buyer]
18 deals from 2016 to 2023, of which 15 closed (83%); 4 deals since 2022. [T:record, K:closed_share, K:recent]
Ranks 9th on the priority list of 10, with a likelihood of 3.7% across 107 buyers scored. [R:rank]

strategic_fit_thesis.title: Adjacent provider record and growth focus, but little in the target's niche
points: Having bought from this kind of seller is a modest factor; 1 deal in the target's own sub-sector and 8 in adjacent provider sub-sectors. [S:own_fit_s, T:record]
High Growth was a motive in 10 of 18 deals, relevant to the target's 11.0% revenue growth. [M:high_growth, X:target]
No open platform in the sub-sector, so the target would be a new position rather than an add-on. [A:angles]

precedent_activity.title: Closest precedents: $187M and $203M deals at 11.2x and 12.2x
points: Quality Medical Group: $187M minority investment, 2022, same sub-sector as the target, 11.2x EV/EBITDA. [D:MA-2022-0350]
Granite Dental Network: $203M platform investment, 2021, 12.2x EV/EBITDA. [D:MA-2021-0439]
8 of 18 deals sit in the $100M-$400M size band; median deal is $88M and the biggest $1,388M. [K:size_band, T:record]

valuation_context.title: Upper-quartile pricing is defensible, but the return at the ask is thin
points: Comparable deals (70): EV/EBITDA of 10.7x at the 25th percentile, 12.8x median and 15.3x at the 75th percentile. [V:comps]
The target's 16.8% margin against a comparable median of 12.9% supports the 75th percentile; TPG's own median paid is 15.7x. [V:comps]
At the ask, IRR is 18.7% against a 20% target; maximum price is $193M at the same exit, $216M at a 15.0x platform exit. [V:lbo]

risk_flags.title: Size stretch
risk_flags.concern: Median deal of $88M is under half the $200M EV. [T:record, X:target]
risk_flags.mitigant: 8 of 18 deals sit in the $100M-$400M size band. [K:size_band]
risk_flags.reality: Reach is proven at $187M and $203M, though the $187M deal was a minority stake. [D:MA-2022-0350, D:MA-2021-0439]

risk_flags.title: Return at the asking price
risk_flags.concern: IRR at the ask of 18.7% is below the 20% target. [V:lbo]
risk_flags.mitigant: A platform exit at 15.0x lifts the maximum price to $216M. [V:lbo]
risk_flags.reality: The bid works only if it underwrites a platform exit, and no open platform exists today. [V:lbo, A:angles]

risk_flags.title: Thin Midwest and own-sub-sector record
risk_flags.concern: Only 1 deal in the target's region; geography is a slight factor against. [S:geo_fit, T:record]
risk_flags.mitigant: It has a Midwest precedent: Metro Medical Associates, 2018. [D:MA-2018-0415]
risk_flags.reality: Just 1 deal in the target's own sub-sector, against 4 in its home Health Insurance. [T:record, K:by_sub_sector]

conviction.rationale: Only 1 deal in the target's own sub-sector and 8 adjacent, no open platform, and a median deal of $88M under half the $200M EV. [C:conviction]
